newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas extends gains with heat, storage buys.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas extends gains with heat, storage buys.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices staged another rally Wednesday as the heat in the West continued to sustain a strong cooling demand and buyers elsewhere packed gas into storage, sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at the Henry Hub were quoted up an average of five to six cents to about $2.38.
In the Midwest, swing prices gained another three cents to the high-$2.20s. Chicago city-gate gas prices edged up a couple of cents to $2.40-2.44.

"They just keep on biting the bullet and paying the price. They just keep on refilling storage," one Midwest trader said, adding he thought buyers went into the month short in anticipation of softer prices in the aftermarket.
In the Permian Basin market, prices rose another 11 cents to $2.35-2.38 in congruence with the rallying electricity market.
Prices in Palo Verde for next-day delivery peak loads were quoted at $110.00-165.00 per megawatt hour.
San Juan basin gas was also several cents higher at $2.28-2.34, while southern California border prices soared into the mid-to-high $2.40s.
In the East, cooler-than-normal weather kept a lid on pricing as New York city gate prices held in the low-$2.50s. Appalachian prices, however, climbed two cents to $2.47-2.51, traders said.
